items.title: 姆巴佩就「中國獨裁者」迷因道歉 背後的資訊真空與「毛澤東熱」
items.description: 因在節目中以「獨裁者」形容已故中國領導人毛澤東，法國足球明星基利安·姆巴佩（麥巴比）近日在中國引發爭議，多家中國大型品牌先後宣佈終止與其合作。姆巴佩發表道歉聲明也不被中國網民接納。
items.content:
姆巴佩就「中國獨裁者」迷因道歉：風波背後的資訊真空與「毛澤東熱」
因訪談中談及一張「中國獨裁者」迷因圖而捲入辱華風波的法國足球明星基利安·姆巴佩（Kylian Mbappé；麥巴比），周二（10月27日）發表聲明，「向所有被我的言論所傷害的人道歉」。這張迷因將他的臉合成到已故中共領導人毛澤東的形象上。
但在聲明發表約20分鐘後，中國足球協會（中國足協）發文稱已與姆巴佩所屬的皇家馬德里俱樂部「嚴正交涉」，要求涉事球員和俱樂部「作出公開正式道歉」。西甲方面與涉事訪談節目《The Bridge》同日亦先後致歉。
在此之前，東鵬飲料、蒙牛乳業等多家中國品牌已以「傷害民族感情」為由宣布終止與姆巴佩的合作或與其劃清界線，中國中央廣播電視總台（總台）亦暫停播出與他相關的賽事內容及廣告。
連串道歉未能平息輿論。微博熱搜上與姆巴佩相關的話題一度佔據前十中的六席，中國外交部發言人也就事件表態。這場風波之所以迅速延燒，與毛澤東在當代中國社會、尤其是年輕世代中的特殊位置密不可分。
球員、節目、西甲接連道歉
10月27日，姆巴佩經認證的X賬號發表聲明：「在近期的一次採訪中，我對一張以我為主角的圖片作出了回應。我的言論欠妥，如今我明白，這些話傷害了中國以及世界各地華人社區的許多人。我向所有被我的言論所傷害的人道歉。這絕非我的本意。我對這個人民及其歷史懷有深深的敬意，我真心感到抱歉。」
聲明以姆巴佩個人公司Interconnected Ventures的信箋發出，發佈時間為歐洲早上、北京時間傍晚，消息傳到中國後旋即登上微博熱搜首位。
約20分鐘後，中國足協在微博發表聲明，稱協會「高度重視」，已第一時間與皇家馬德里俱樂部「進行嚴正交涉，要求涉事球員和皇家馬德里俱樂部作出公開正式道歉」。聲明又說：「中國足協堅決反對任何傷害中國人民感情的言論。國際知名運動員尤其應當嚴守底線、理性發聲，珍惜自身公眾影響力。」
同日晚上，西甲聯賽在微博及X的官方帳號同步發佈道歉文，表示「對於基利安·姆巴佩近期言論對中國球迷帶來的冒犯與傷害，西甲聯盟深感遺憾。相關言論屬於球員個人表達，絕不代表西甲聯盟的立場」。文中又稱：「我們始終對中國、各相關機構及中國人民懷有深切的敬意，也無比珍惜數百萬中國球迷每週給予我們的關注與支持。」
《The Bridge》節目同日在Instagram限時動態致歉，承認此前發佈了相關訪談片段：「我們深深遺憾這段片段冒犯了中國和世界其他地方的人。」西甲主席哈維爾·特巴斯（Javier Tebas）其後亦發聲明稱，已與中國駐西班牙大使姚敬會面，討論風波並尋求解決方案。央視體育方面則以「聽其言更觀其行」回應，表示希望西甲和相關人士「痛改前非」。
連番表態在民間收效甚微。西甲道歉文的微博評論區裡，獲最多點讚的是一條福建用戶的留言：「他忘記出生了嗎，就幾十年沒採棉花而已。」X平台上則有用戶回應：「因為稱呼一個獨裁者是獨裁者而道歉嗎？哈哈。」在新浪新聞的相關帖文下，一位江蘇網民說：「他不是知道錯了，他是知道怕了，沒處撈錢了。」一位河北網民說：「不接受，讓世界人們知道知道教員在中國人心中的份量！」
涉及毛澤東的「迷因圖」
風波源於10月26日起在Reddit、X（前稱Twitter）及Threads等社交平台廣泛流傳的一段訪談片段。影片顯示，姆巴佩在法國網絡訪談節目《The Bridge》中，被問到「以自己頭像製作的網絡迷因圖（meme，中國大陸也稱『梗圖』）中，哪一個最令你發笑」時表示，最好笑的是有人將他的臉合成到一名「中國獨裁者」的照片上，並稱自己與朋友打電玩時經常使用這張圖。
姆巴佩在回答中並未點名。不過，節目後期製作加入了一張將他的面孔與毛澤東形象合成的圖片，不少觀眾因此認為，他所指的正是毛澤東。
BBC未能獨立核實該訪談的錄製及發佈時間。《The Bridge》官方社交媒體帳號已無法找到相關片段，節目網站亦未提供重播。
姆巴佩現效力西甲皇家馬德里，並擔任法國國家隊隊長。他曾協助法國隊奪得2018年世界盃冠軍，並在2022年世界盃決賽上演帽子戲法，被廣泛視為當今足壇最具影響力和商業價值的球員之一。在中國市場，他亦曾長期受品牌青睞，先後與蒙牛、東鵬飲料、小紅書等企業合作。
品牌解約、官方施壓
訪談片段持續發酵後，東鵬飲料集團於10月27日率先發表聲明，宣布終止與姆巴佩的合作，稱公司「堅決反對、零容忍傷害民族感情的行為」。蒙牛乳業及妙可藍多其後亦相繼宣布解除與他的合作關係。
生活分享平台小紅書同樣發表聲明，反對任何傷害民族感情的言行，同時澄清與姆巴佩的商業合作已於2024年12月31日結束，目前正對相關宣傳物料進行排查及下架。總台同日下午表示，由於姆巴佩涉及「涉華嚴重負面行為」，已自本周一起暫停播出涉及他的西甲聯賽及相關內容，所有以其為主角的商業廣告亦同步下架。
中國外交部也加入評論。發言人郭嘉昆10月27日在例行記者會上回應相關提問時說：「我們注意到有關報導。傷害中國人民感情的言行自然會遭到中國社會各界的共同抵制。」
輿論場上，北京廣播電視台旗下《北京時間》發佈的社論「姆巴佩深知被羞辱的滋味卻不懂尊重」一度位居熱搜榜首。社論提及姆巴佩今年7月世界盃期間遭受種族歧視的經歷：當時，巴拉圭參議員塞萊斯特·阿馬里利亞（Celeste Amarilla）在網絡上稱他是「一個被殖民的喀麥隆人，假裝自己是法國人，充滿怨氣、暴發戶、傲慢而醜陋」，姆巴佩本人及法國足協曾直接回擊，稱有關言論「令人髮指、不可接受」。
社論指出，他遭受的種族歧視與其此次言論性質相似，他不應一邊賺中國人的錢，一邊傷害中國人的感情。
近年，因被中國輿論認定「傷害民族感情」而付出商業代價的事件並不罕見。2021年，快時尚品牌H&M因就新疆強迫勞動問題發表聲明，在中國遭遇大規模抵制，多個地圖及電商平台一度將其下架，多名中國藝人宣布終止合作；法國奢侈品牌Dior亦曾因廣告中使用被部分網民稱為「眯眯眼」的模特形象捲入爭議，被批評醜化中國人。這類爭議往往隨網絡輿論升溫，迅速蔓延至商業層面。
「教員」、資訊真空與「毛澤東熱」
在微博、抖音等平台上，不少網民仍在發問：姆巴佩到底說了什麼？事件緣由為何？
中國最大的足球資訊平台懂球帝10月26日晚上發文稱，由於內容「涉及對中國和中國人民的傷害」，平台選擇不予翻譯，同時呼籲球迷理性討論，避免過激言論。冷處理反而加劇了好奇：有擅長「翻牆」的網民找到訪談原片，在社交平台兜售片段，吸引好奇者付費觀看。
而在聲討姆巴佩的輿論中，一種聲音憤怒於「姆巴佩傷害了中國人民感情」這一官方敘事，隨之搖旗吶喊；另一種則是自己看過爭議影片的網民，質問「他怎麼敢說我們教員？」。在中國年輕人的網絡語境中，「教員」是對毛澤東的代稱。
姆巴佩風波因此已不止是一場圍繞球星言論的輿論事件，同時折射出毛澤東在當代中國社會中的特殊位置。
毛澤東雖已去世50年，但他對今日中國的影響仍在放大，尤其在活躍於網絡的年輕人之中。BBC中文此前曾報導，在當代中國年輕人的網絡文化中，毛澤東正經歷一輪顯著的「回潮」：影片平台Bilibili（B站）上的毛澤東相關影片，動輒錄得數百萬播放量；《毛澤東選集》連續多年位居清華大學圖書館年度借閱榜首。毛澤東已重新進入「Z世代」的日常政治語言。
值得注意的是，隨著中國經濟增速放緩，就業、房價、性別等社會矛盾日益突出，毛澤東關於階級、平等與反資本支配的論述，被一些年輕人視為理解自身處境的一套簡明而有力的解釋框架。他在當代中國社會中的意義，早已超出官方的歷史定位本身。

items.title: 劉延東逝世：「紅二代」「團派」背景，政治局裡少見的女性身影
items.description: 劉延東的逝世提醒外界一個現象：從吳儀、劉延東到孫春蘭，中共中央政治局曾連續20年保持至少一名女性委員，直到2022年「二十大」中斷，權力核心再無女性。
items.content:
劉延東逝世：「紅二代」「團派」背景，政治局裡少見的女性身影
官方新華社星期三（10月28日）公布，中國國務院前副總理劉延東因病在北京逝世，享年81歲。
新華社的報導稱其為「中國共產黨的優秀黨員，久經考驗的忠誠的共產主義戰士，我黨統一戰線工作和我國教育科技、醫療衛生、婦女兒童工作的傑出領導人」。
劉延東曾在2007年至2017年連續兩屆擔任中共中央政治局委員，2008年出任國務委員，2013年升任國務院副總理，2018年退休。她是改革開放後第二位女性政治局委員，以及中共建政後第四位女性副總理（此前三人是吳桂賢、陳慕華、吳儀）。
在中共高層，劉延東是少數同時擁有革命幹部家庭、共青團和統戰系統背景的領導人。「紅二代」與「團派」是她仕途上最鮮明的兩個標籤，她與香港亦淵源頗深。
她的逝世，也提醒外界一個現象：從吳儀、劉延東到孫春蘭，中共政治局曾連續20年保持至少一名女性委員，直到2022年中共「二十大」中斷，再無女性政治局委員。
「紅二代」：與江澤民父輩的淵源
劉延東的第一個標籤，是「紅二代」。
她1945年11月出生，籍貫江蘇南通。父親劉瑞龍是中共早期革命幹部，曾參與創建中國工農紅軍第十四軍（紅十四軍），後來擔任解放軍第三野戰軍後勤司令兼政治委員，深度參與國共內戰。
中共建政後，劉瑞龍出任農業部常務副部長。文化大革命期間，他受到迫害，被關押五年，文革結束後才重返農業部工作。
這一家庭背景，使劉延東被外界歸入革命幹部後代組成的「紅二代」。不過，劉瑞龍生前最高職位為副部級，未及「黨和國家領導人」之列。
此外，已故中共中央總書記江澤民的養父江上青也與劉家淵源甚深。官方資料記述，江上青1927年考入南通中學高中部，「受劉瑞龍、顧民元革命思想影響」，當年加入共青團，此後到上海求學，並於1929年加入共產黨。
「團派」：從團中央書記到國務院副總理
劉延東的第二個標籤，是「團派」。
1964年，劉延東進入清華大學工程化學系學習，畢業後先後在河北唐山和北京的化工廠工作，從工人、技術員逐步進入工廠黨委領導層。
1980年，她調入中共北京市委組織部，隨後出任朝陽區委副書記。同一時期升任北京區委副書記的，還有中共元老陳雲之子陳元、陳毅之子陳昊蘇。
1982年，劉延東進入中國共產主義青年團中央委員會（共青團中央），先後擔任書記處書記、常務書記，以及全國青聯副主席、主席，在這一系統工作至1991年。
這段經歷，使她經常被外界歸入「團派」——這並非中共的正式組織名稱，而是外界用來描述具有共青團任職經歷、尤其與胡錦濤存在工作聯繫的一批官員，李克強、胡春華等都是代表人物。中共「二十大」後，隨著習近平開啟第三個中央總書記任期，「團派」全面退出中央政治局，已十分式微。
1991年，正值江澤民執政時期，劉延東離開共青團，轉任中共中央統一戰線工作部副部長，2002年後晉升統戰部部長。
2007年中共「十七大」，劉延東躋身中央政治局，成為改革開放後第二位女性政治局委員，首位是吳儀。2012年中共「十八大」，她連任政治局委員，成為繼周恩來遺孀鄧穎超之後，中共歷史上第二位連任政治局委員的女性。
2013年「兩會」，劉延東出任國務院副總理。2015年，她還兼任中國足球改革領導小組組長——這是其中一個習近平相當重視的項目。
與香港聯繫緊密
劉延東與香港的工作聯繫，主要貫穿她在統戰部和國務院任職的時期。
當時正值香港特區與中央政府關係融洽之時，劉延東多次訪問香港。2004年5月，她訪港出席法門寺佛指舍利抵港的相關活動，並會見香港各界親建制人士。2009年12月，她出席香港東亞運動會開幕式，並到香港大學出席活動。
此外，劉延東的女兒楊帆長期在香港工作。
彭博社曾報導，楊帆2015年至2020年在招商證券國際擔任行政總裁，2020年起出任瑞銀亞洲全球銀行業務主席，常駐香港，是該行近年來為拓展中國業務而聘請的多位知名業務拓展專才之一，2022年底因個人原因離職。
政治局女性席位的中斷
已故中共領導人毛澤東曾說「婦女能頂半邊天」，但在毛時代，女性官員少之又少，能夠進入政治局的，往往憑藉的是身份而非能力，例如江青（毛澤東妻子）、葉群（林彪妻子）和鄧穎超（周恩來妻子）。
2002年，吳儀成為改革開放後首位女性政治局委員。此後20年，劉延東、孫春蘭先後入局，政治局始終保持至少一名女性成員。
三位女性委員的職務軌跡頗為相似：先後擔任副總理，主要分管教育、衛生、科技等領域。其中，吳儀和孫春蘭分別在薩斯（SARS；非典型肺炎／沙士）和新冠疫情（COVID-19 pandemic）期間主導了防疫工作。
直到2022年中共「二十大」，24人的政治局名單中沒有女性，這一格局戛然而止。
也有觀點認為，沒有女性入局是基於現實考量。新冠疫情和中美「科技戰」，令傳統上由女性副總理分管的科技和衛生領域變得更為重要。而此前被看好的諶貽琴長期在貴州任職，缺乏科技、衛生方面的資歷，最終僅出任國務委員。
「二十大」後，科技工作交由躋身「七常委」之列的副總理丁薛祥分管。這一安排本身，便體現了相關工作的重要性。

items.title: 西班牙列車相撞至少68死：我們目前已知甚麼？
items.description: 西班牙兩列載有逾500名乘客的高速列車相撞。該國交通部長表示，電腦系統故障導致列車一度停駛，但控制中心其後在「令人費解的情況下」，沒有實施速度限制而允許列車恢復行駛，最終釀成事故。
items.content:
西班牙列車相撞至少68死：我們目前已知甚麼？
  - Author, 黃瑋殷（Vicky Wong）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
西班牙首都馬德里以南周三（10月28日）早上發生兩列火車相撞事故。
鐵路基建管理公司Adif表示，事故涉及西班牙國家鐵路公司Renfe及私營高鐵公司Iryo的列車，兩列車均行駛馬德里至塞維利亞（Seville）路線。
目前已確認至少68人在事故中死亡。
以下是目前已知的事故詳情。
在何時何地發生？
兩列列車於當地時間早上9時（格林尼治標準時間早上8時）過後不久，在莫拉（Mora）和奧爾加斯（Orgaz）兩個市鎮之間相撞，事故地點位於馬德里以南約140公里（100英里）。
事故發生時，一列從馬德里開往西班牙南部的高速列車，撞上另一列相信當時停在路軌上的列車。撞擊導致至少兩節車廂翻落路堤。
西班牙廣播電視公司RTVE引述交通部表示，Renfe列車從後撞上Iryo列車。
鐵路基建管理公司Adif表示，這條路線的所有列車已在沿途車站停駛。
Renfe表示，馬德里、雷阿爾城（Ciudad Real）及安達盧西亞（Andalusia）之間的列車服務仍然暫停。
其中一列列車上的一名乘客向當地傳媒表示，列車開出約40分鐘後，突然發生猛烈撞擊。
事故原因
Iryo表示，旗下列車「遭一列Renfe列車從後撞上」，事故原因「目前仍未查明」。
西班牙交通部長奧斯卡·普恩特（Oscar Puente）表示，電腦系統故障導致六列原本正在行駛的列車最初被迫停駛，包括其後相撞的兩列列車。
他說：「當系統發生故障時，控制中心便會接管。」他補充說，是控制中心決定讓列車恢復行駛，而且沒有施加任何速度限制。
普恩特表示，這項決定是在「令人費解的情況下」作出的，結果導致Renfe列車撞上前方停在路軌上的Iryo列車。
兩列列車上有多少乘客？
據信兩列列車合共有超過500人在車上。
卡斯蒂利亞－拉曼恰自治區（Castilla-La Mancha）政府發言人埃絲特·帕迪利亞（Esther Padilla）向西班牙電視台TVE表示，Iryo營運的列車載有146名乘客及一名嬰兒，而Renfe列車則載有397名乘客。
據報，一名前政府部長亦是失蹤者之一。
西班牙企業組織聯合會（CEOE）在社交平台X發文表示，該組織旗下基金會的負責人、前部長法蒂瑪·巴涅斯（Fátima Báñez）當時正在其中一列涉事列車上。
卡斯蒂利亞－拉曼恰自治區主席埃米利亞諾·加西亞－帕赫（Emiliano García-Page）向當地傳媒表示，目前已確認68人死亡。
自治區政府主席另外向西班牙傳媒表示，死亡人數可能進一步上升。
當局表示，80名傷者正接受治療，其中50人傷勢嚴重，另有15人情況危殆。
當局如何應對？
西班牙首相桑切斯（Pedro Sánchez）表示，他對托萊多發生的嚴重列車事故感到「震驚」。
桑切斯在社交平台X發文表示：「我一直與交通部長及卡斯蒂利亞－拉曼恰自治區主席保持密切聯繫。」
他補充說，緊急救援人員正與各相關部門協調，在現場協助受影響人士並確保他們的安全。
他說：「我向所有遇難者及其家屬致以關懷、慰問和支持。」
桑切斯及其他西班牙政界人士已取消周三所有公開活動，包括為下月國會選舉進行的競選活動。
西班牙王室在X發文表示，對事故感到「震驚和憂慮」，並向遇難者家屬及其他受事故影響的人士致以慰問。
歐盟一名發言人表示，如有需要，歐盟隨時準備向西班牙提供援助。
當局正展開大規模緊急救援行動，消防隊及直升機已趕赴事故現場。
西班牙通訊社報道，當地醫院因應大批事故傷者送院，已暫停原定的手術。
馬德里一間輸血中心亦緊急呼籲民眾捐血。馬德里輸血中心（Centro de Transfusión）在X發文表示，由於醫療需求可能突然大增，因此發出「緊急」捐血呼籲。
據報，托萊多、雷阿爾城及聖胡安堡（Alcázar de San Juan）的醫療設施，隨着事故傷者陸續送抵，已取消原定的醫療程序。
這是西班牙今年第二宗涉及高速鐵路的重大致命事故。
今年1月，西班牙南部一列高速列車出軌，尾部車廂衝入另一列由國營鐵路公司Renfe營運的列車行駛路線，造成46人死亡。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.content:
台灣「九合一」選舉五大看點：「洋流」能否撼動台北？誰在卡位2028大選？
  - Author, 呂嘉鴻
  - Role, BBC中文記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 5 分鐘
台灣「九合一」地方選舉將於11月底舉行，台北首都之戰，執政民進黨候選人沈伯洋異軍突起，與代表國民黨的現任市長蔣萬安在民調中互有高下。
由於台北市長一直是台灣總統大位「跳板」，使這場選戰成為關注熱點。
此外，在海峽另一端，北京同樣出手。近日，大陸國台辦公開抨擊沈伯洋為「台獨頑固份子」並點名其家人。
中共是否介入台灣選舉？ 這次選舉將如何影響賴清德與國民黨主席鄭麗文的政治能量？捲土重來、希望藉著地方議員選舉有所斬獲的小黨，此次結盟能否在主流政黨夾殺中突圍而出？
BBC中文採訪台灣議題專家，整理出此次選舉值得關注的五大看點。
看點一：「洋流」海嘯，還是曇花一現？
身兼立法委員和台北大學副教授的沈伯洋，選情從不被看好到明顯回升，在台灣政壇掀起千層浪，輿論稱為「洋流」現象。
事實上，根據台灣TVBS民調中心10月初公布的調查，蔣萬安支持度為49%、沈伯洋為41%，雙方差距已從今年5月下旬約28個百分點，大幅縮小至8個百分點，台北選情愈發激烈。而新成立的台北信民兩岸研究協會10月20日公布的台北市長選舉民調中，沈伯洋以50.3%支持度領先蔣萬安的33.3%。
兩份民調何以差別如此顯著？
信民協會贊助人曹興誠為知名綠營支持者，與沈伯洋同被中國列為「台獨頑固份子」；TVBS舊稱無線衛星電視台，曾是香港無線電視（TVB）子公司，台灣輿論傾向將其視為「親藍」媒體。
對此，台灣資深媒體人黃暐瀚稱「民調是一時一地，可以注意，不必在意。」但他又說，這幾次台北市民調結果，沈伯洋攀升而蔣萬安下滑的「趨勢」浮現。
外界開始聚焦：這股動能是否能真正「破圈」、外溢到其他縣市，並轉化為實質投票？
而面對「洋流」聲勢，蔣萬安陣營以市政成績回應。
他在台灣政論節目呼籲支持者「勇敢站出來」，並肯定自己執掌台北市政府四年來的政績。他還數次強調台北市在「幸福城市」評比連續兩年獲得六都第一，團隊一路走來都抱持「戰戰兢兢」的態度。
台灣台北大學公共行政暨政策學系劉嘉薇教授向BBC中文分析，沈伯洋「這股選情的提升是否可以轉化成支持度，還需要進一步觀察。」
劉嘉薇解釋，原因是政治冷漠的選民未必瞭解沈伯洋，但熱衷政治的選民對相關事件相當熟悉：「他們記得沈伯洋過去在『大罷免』的積極參與、在立法院問政時的『肢體衝突』的形象，以及鮮明的『台獨』立場。」
然而，一位戶籍在大安區，在外商會計事務所上班的黃小姐則向BBC中文表示，她這次會把選票投給沈伯洋，原因是「沈先生在政策論述及配套措施清楚並有說服力。作為一個挑戰者，有備而來。」
黃小姐說，在兒童虐待及食安等問題，她對現任市府團隊失去信心。
相反地，一位居住在紐約的台僑接受台灣自媒體採訪說，他一定會回台灣投給蔣萬安，他認為蔣萬安對台北市的發展很有想法，另一位在法拉盛受訪的移居美國的女士也強調，台北市政府在蔣萬安領導下行政效率高，值得她信任。
看點二：北京會介入台灣地方選舉嗎？
研究認知作戰以及境外勢力的分析人士指出，AI深偽、假訊息、社交媒體定向攻擊特定候選人、假民調、經濟利誘等，是常見的境外勢力介入其他國家或對手的手段。
中國大陸國務院台灣事務辦公室也在最近出招。
據官媒新華社報導，國台辦發言人陳斌華在10月14日答問直接點名沈伯洋的父親，稱其為躲避制裁，以另一家公司名義，繼續同中國大陸相關企業做生意，「從中謀取經濟利益。」
陳斌華稱：「沈伯洋一邊鼓噪『反中抗中』、阻礙兩岸交流合作，一邊會同親屬想方設法從大陸賺錢，醜陋行徑令人不齒。」
對此，美國智庫太平洋論壇（Pacific Forum）兼任資深研究員藍若思教授（Elizabeth Larus）向BBC中文指出，她訪問的親民進黨學者與社運人士，以及台北國防部的一些官員表示，中共正運用「認知作戰」來影響台灣選民。
藍若思說，她的研究對象向她表示中共已建立超過100個假新聞網站，企圖影響選舉。
「這些網站刻意在選民心中播下疑慮，質疑美國是否會支持或防衛台灣，或是操弄選民對『抵抗中國是徒勞無功』的恐懼，藉此促使選民拒絕民進黨候選人。」她說。
美國哈佛大學政府系講師索羅卡博士 （George Soroka）過去曾向BBC中文表示，所謂「非民主」國家部署的宣傳攻勢向來要更凌厲許多。
他觀察到北京採用了許多與莫斯科相似手法，特別是近年利用對過往歷史事件的選擇性解讀，來增加其對台灣和南海等地區主張的合理性。
台灣事實查核中心（TFC）2025年也出版一份調查報告聚焦在台灣防衛安全焦慮相關假訊息。
該報告稱，許多挪用台灣戲劇或廣告畫面，最早可追溯到中國微博、抖音等平台，再流傳到臉書（Facebook）、TikTok等。事件驅動的敘事（如恢復軍審）則常由台灣本地政治人物或「小型」網紅放大。
對此，美國聖湯瑪斯大學教授葉耀元則在個人網站分析，此次台灣選舉，中共的認知作戰雖未必會直接改變選民投票立場，但有加深台灣社會對立與兩極化的效果。
看點三：最大「票倉」的關鍵對決與「政二代」面臨考驗
人口400萬，300多萬選民，新北市的這兩組數字皆為全台之冠。
此次新北市長選舉由民進黨現任立委蘇巧慧對上曾擔任新北市及高雄市副市長的國民黨李四川。
許多評論稱，新北市中間選民比例高，民調互有領先，被視為決定全國版圖勝負的指標戰場。
綜合各方數據顯示，李四川在藍營基本盤與特定族群中擁有較高凝聚力，蘇巧慧則在年輕選民中獲得青睞，雙方選情仍呈拉鋸狀態。
蘇巧慧是前行政院長、前台北縣長蘇貞昌之女，國民黨高雄市長參選人柯志恩之父，為前屏東縣長柯文福；民進黨新竹縣長參選人鄭朝方之父，為國民黨籍前新竹縣長鄭永金。
因此，有分析稱，這些中壯派的政治人物回到地方爭取首長大位，折射出台灣政治家族的延續與更新。
有些「政二代」選擇跨出家族的黨派路線，如鄭朝方強調自己早在學生時期即確立「台派」立場，蘇巧慧則稱自己為「民主二代」，也有如同台中顏家及雲林張家，始終是國民黨在當地派系的中流砥柱。
受訪專家稱，這凸顯台灣地方政治中「政二代」的資源、形象優勢與包袱並存的處境。
譬如，這次選舉幾位熱門的政二代候選人雙親都未高調站台。也有候選人幕僚向BBC中文婉拒談論政二代議題，背後是希望凸顯「靠自己，不靠爸媽」。
台灣東海大學政治學系張峻豪向BBC中文強調，台灣民主化經歷一段時間，因此政二代是資產還是包袱還不一定。仍需要從政二代自己的表現，包含在地方的經營夠不夠扎實，在議會或立院的表現來判斷。
換言之，政二代無法「無縫接軌」的從家族長輩傳承中拿下選票。
以蘇巧慧為例，張峻豪分析蘇女士此次能與政治實力龐大的李四川一較高下，主要在於她自己長年的地方經營，年輕形象以及洋流外溢有關。
但張峻豪也表示蘇貞昌的「老縣長」資歷，與地方的長期良好關係，也帶給女兒優勢。
或許，在新北市選情的膠著，正是這波世代交替在最大票倉的具體呈現。
看點四：「無大台」的台灣小黨能在地方選舉突圍嗎？
全台灣約有60萬名首投族，許多專家都表示，歷次選舉以來，緊繃的選區勝負往往取決於中間選民與投票率。
因此，有專家指出，這次地方選舉多數候選人聚焦住房、交通、經濟、地方治理等民生問題，而非直接以「抗中保台」為主軸。
小黨如何在民生議題打動選民，尋求突破也成為焦點。
譬如時代力量、台灣綠黨、小民參政歐巴桑聯盟與台灣基進組成「台灣前進」陣線，承諾選區不重疊、集中資源，試圖在基層議會層級建立「本土第三勢力」。
在台北市文山區擔任無黨籍里長八年的陳峙穎，此次接受時代力量提名，參與北市市議員選舉，他強調唯有出身基層的人，才知道每天為房租、物價、醫療、交通與工作奔波的人在想什麼。
在高雄，從時代力量退黨加入民眾黨的前議員林于凱，在當地發起行人路權促進會專注路權交通問題，此次再次加入選戰希望以民生議題重返議會。
分析小黨困境，台灣大學政治系王業立教授曾指出，台灣社會長期有第三勢力存在的空間，卻往往互相取而代之，近期甚至有「淘汰率」提高、生命週期變短的趨勢。
長期觀察台灣小黨發展，王教授發現多數小黨分裂自藍綠，因此意識形態上難以完全獨立，又或者資源有限導致黨內內鬥逐漸失去政治能量。
此外，台灣的選舉制度也不利小黨。以台灣不分區立委來說，若政黨票得票率低於5%，該政黨無法獲得任何不分區立委席次，要超過3%的得票率才有政黨補助金。
張峻豪教授便告訴BBC中文，即便是縣市議員的地方政治工作，都需要穩定經營蹲點，才能在地方獲得支持。
小黨便因為欠缺資源補助，說到底缺錢也缺人去經營地方，張教授因此並不看好小黨這次在選舉能有滿意的成績。
唯一例外的是台灣社會民主黨的苗博雅，自2018年當選台北市市議員以來，連任至今，在當地廣獲中產階級及學生選民支持。
看點五：賴清德與鄭麗文首次交手 牽動2028大選佈局
這場選舉被視為總統賴清德的執政「期中考」，也是上任一年的國民黨主席鄭麗文的重要考驗。
美國《外交家》（The Diplomat）雜誌兩位台灣研究者投書稱，地方選舉本質是地方議題，不應直接解讀為對賴清德或全國政治的公投。
但兩位作者認為，賴清德與鄭麗文都是高度兩極化人物，地方選戰中多刻意迴避兩人形象，若國民黨表現不佳，身為潛在候選人的鄭麗文將面臨黨內壓力，2028總統初選也會更複雜。
藍若思則強調「所有政治都是地方政治」認同此次九合一選舉關乎台灣國內政治與地方現實的程度，遠超過兩岸關係。
半年前剛結束台灣訪問的藍若思指出，前總統蔡英文在2022年地方選舉最後幾週大力強調中國因素，結果執政民進黨在北部縣市長候選人全數落敗，即是明證。

items.title: Anthropic 重磅上市——目前我們知道的五件驚人信息
items.description: Anthropic 的招股說明書長達355頁，其中包含大量從未披露過的公司資訊。
items.content:
Anthropic 重磅上市——目前我們知道的五件驚人信息
  - Author, 卡莉·海斯 （Kali Hays）
  - Role, BBC科技記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
人工智慧（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智能）公司 Anthropic 公佈了其美國股市上市所需文件，這次招股市場期盼已久。
長達335頁的文件揭露了這家 Claude 聊天機器人所有者如何賺錢、把錢花在哪裡，以及由誰控制等新細節。
Anthropic 也詳細說明了它認為 AI 技術可能帶來的一些風險，包括可能奪取人命。這些資訊與該技術宣稱的諸多好處並列呈現。
以下是這份文件中值得關注的五個重點。
1. 「世界末日」是一種職業風險
每家上市公司都必須告訴潛在投資者，事情可能如何出錯。
不過，Anthropic 的「風險因素」相當獨特，它還披露了其正在開發的 AI 技術如何可能導致全人類的滅亡。
Anthropic 表示：「如果沒有適當的保障、監督和安全措施來開發、部署和運作，足夠先進的 AI 系統可能對人類構成災難性或存在性風險。」
報告又指出，不到一年前，一個 Anthropic 相信由中國支持的駭客組織「操縱」了Claude，成功入侵多個機構，包括大型科技公司、金融機構、化學製造公司和政府機關。
但，Anthropic 表示，其成功取決於持續「開發、改進和部署最先進、最強大和最有用的AI模型」的能力。
此外，對這項能力最重大的風險之一，是 Anthropic 能否取得所需的基礎設施，包括電腦晶片和資料中心，以建立、訓練和運作支撐其技術的模型。
2. 這家公司正火速「燒錢」
Anthropic 尚未公布其股票上市的目標股價。
市場普遍預期該公司上市時的市值將達到2萬億美元（13.34萬億元人民幣；64.8兆元新台幣）或更高，成為史上最大的股票上市案。
但這個數字將深受其財務表現影響。
Anthropic 在今年上半年虧損807億美元（5,381億元人民幣；2.62兆元新台幣），是2025年全年虧損的兩倍。該公司在這六個月的整體營收為162億美元。
雖然營收正快速上升，但距離損益平衡仍有很長的路要走。
Mergermarket 股權資本市場聯合主管赫伯爾（Troy Hooper）強調 Anthropic 的營收成長「非凡」，但他也補充說，投資者對承諾巨大未來回報的科技公司，已不如幾個月前那麼寬容。
此外，Anthropic 的債務狀況也不清楚，因為它有大量與某些形式投資相關的會計費用。
赫伯爾補充說：「因此，投資者目前還不清楚 Anthropic 的潛在獲利能力，也不知道其現金產生速度是否足以支撐業務擴張。」
3. 但幸運的是，公司現金充裕
儘管虧損，Anthropic 手上仍有大量現金。
以1316億美元計算，其幾乎所有現金都被定義為「營運資金」，意味著它可以用來支付日常營運。
目前，Anthropic 手上的現金比 Meta 和谷歌（Google）加起來還多。
但是，隨著與其他 AI 巨頭激烈爭奪頂尖人才和運算能力，Anthropic 的成本可能上升。光是租用數據中心，今年迄今已讓該公司花費3214億美元。
赫伯爾分析，如此龐大的成本預計還會增加。即使有這種現金量，也不足以維持其業務成長。
他說，任何投資 Anthropic 的人「將是為未來的主導地位付費，而非現在的經濟效益」。
4. Anthropic 依賴少數幾家大客戶
Anthropic 認為其技術有無數種銷售給客戶的方式。該公司目前業務的很大一部分來自僅250個主要企業客戶，這些客戶過去一年至少支付了1000萬美元。
更小的數字——僅五個企業客戶——佔了其目前業務的四分之一。
Founder ETF投資組合經理孟那翰（Michael Monaghan）指出，「許多 Anthropic 的頂級客戶沒有長期合約」。
這種業務集中度讓 Anthropic 依賴一小部分付費客戶來支撐成長，且沒有保證這種情況會持續。Anthropic 也與 Google 和亞馬遜（Amazon）等公司有企業合作關係，而這兩家公司同時也是其投資者「和競爭對手」。
對此，孟那翰認為這在未來可能產生潛在的商業衝突。
Anthropic 則稱整體企業客戶群成長迅速，從去年約1500個增加到今年近1.2萬個。該公司的成長策略的一部分是免費提供 Claude 工具，然後努力「隨著時間將這些用戶轉化為付費客戶」。
該公司又稱這項策略讓 Claude 成為「史上企業採用速度最快的技術」。
5. 人工智慧可望為世界帶來「非凡」的益處
儘管 Anthropic 已說明 AI 帶來的所有風險，它也重申 AI 將產生「非凡」好處。
該公司說：「實現我們的使命，意味著世界能獲得前沿 AI 的巨大好處，同時減輕最重大的風險。」
該使命被定義為：「負責任地開發和維護先進 AI，以利人類的長期利益。」
「我們不會僅根據商業機會或研究新穎性來追求專案；我們的努力必須推進我們的使命。」
這些假設的好處包括醫療保健的進步，例如開發針對疾病的客製化治療和改善疾病檢測、量身定制的教育和法律建議，以及更高效的電網和電池。
再者，數十年的科學進步可能被壓縮到幾年內，加速藥物發現、疾病檢測和個人化療法的交付。
Anthropic 表示，AI 可以提供個人化教育以及專家級的財務和法律建議，推進電網和電池設計以提高效率和可靠性，並幫助「發展中世界」建立更多技術能力。
該公司說：「最終，我們相信前沿AI將有助於推動全球經濟增長。」
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 西班牙高铁再酿惨剧  追尾脱轨至少64人遇难
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/西班牙高铁再酿惨剧-追尾脱轨至少64人遇难/a-79789821?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 周三上午，西班牙中部托莱多省乌尔达附近，一列国有RENFE高铁追尾一列停车的私营IRYO列车，两节车厢脱轨跌下路堤，至少64人死亡、80人受伤。铁路工会质疑，市场自由化后客流激增，线路维护未能跟上。
items.content:
西班牙高铁再酿惨剧 追尾脱轨至少64人遇难
2026年10月28日
（德国之声中文网）周三（10月28日）西班牙中部发生高速列车追尾事故，至少64人遇难，80人受伤。救援人员仍在残骸中搜寻幸存者和遇难者遗体。
停驶列车遭后车追尾
据美联社和德新社报道，事故发生在马德里以南约130公里、托莱多省乌尔达（Urda）与洛斯耶韦内斯（Los Yebenes）两镇之间的一段平坦路段，周围是橄榄树田。
两列高速列车同向行驶，均从马德里驶往南部的安达卢西亚。据西班牙铁路基础设施管理局（ADIF）的消息人士对当地媒体透露，私营铁路公司IRYO的列车因不明原因停车，上午9时前不久，被国有铁路公司RENFE的列车从后方追尾。据西班牙公共广播公司RTVE报道，IRYO列车有两节车厢脱轨，跌下铁路路堤。一节车厢被撞成金属碎片，残骸散落在碎石坡上。
卡斯蒂利亚-拉曼恰自治区政府发言人帕迪利亚（Esther Padilla）说，IRYO列车上有146名乘客和一名婴儿，RENFE列车上有397人。事故原因尚不清楚。马德里、雷阿尔城和安达卢西亚之间的铁路服务已经暂停。
据美联社报道，RENFE列车上的一名乘客对西班牙国家电视台（TVE）说，列车曾短暂停下，随后重新启动，接着就发生了撞击。他说，车厢向一侧倾斜，像要翻倒一样，行李和手机全都飞了起来。
救援与各方反应
西班牙卫生大臣加西亚（Monica Garcia）说，救援人员正集中力量处理受损最严重的两节车厢，伤者被送往该地区多家医院。"这是一次高速撞击，所以我们预计这将是一场悲剧，"她说。一支军队应急旅已被派往现场协助救援，救护车和医疗直升机往返转运伤者，未受伤的乘客则乘大巴离开。乌尔达镇镇长加兰（Manuel Galan）说，民防部门已要求镇政府准备一座体育馆，用于救治伤员。
IRYO是一家意大利资本控股的公司。该公司表示，已启动安全预案，并与当局密切合作。
西班牙首相桑切斯取消原有日程，专注处理事故，他在X上表示对这起严重事故"深感震惊"。桑切斯将在下个月迎来全国大选。国王费利佩六世和王后莱蒂齐亚表示深感悲痛，向遇难者家属和伤者致以慰问。欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩说："今天，欧洲与你们一同哀悼。"西班牙足球协会推迟了原定当天举行的全部24场国王杯比赛。
铁路网络开放后维护是否跟上？
这是西班牙今年第二起重大铁路事故，也涉及同样的两家公司。今年1月，在南部阿达穆斯附近，一列IRYO列车脱轨，撞上迎面驶来的RENFE列车，造成46人死亡。那是西班牙自2013年80人遇难的铁路事故以来最惨重的一次，曾动摇了公众对西班牙高铁系统的信心。
过去几十年，西班牙在高铁上投入巨资。据国际铁路联盟统计，西班牙在30多年间铺设了约3900公里高铁线路，总裡程仅次于中国。西班牙直到最近才向私营公司开放铁路网络，IRYO于2022年开始在西班牙运营。
西班牙铁路工人工会发言人罗德里格斯（Joan Rodriguez）对西班牙国家电视台表示，自由化带来的客流增加，给铁路基础设施造成了额外压力。他说，工会认为高铁客运自由化的同时，线路并未得到了必要的维护；他并不是说这是事故的决定性因素，但铁路网络使用量增加是需要考虑的因素。

items.title: 以默茨名字命名：新加坡的兰花外交
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/以默茨名字命名：新加坡的兰花外交/a-79789658?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 德国总理默茨访问新加坡期间，获得一项当地外交传统中的特殊礼遇：一种新培育的兰花以他的名字命名。
items.content:
以默茨名字命名：新加坡的兰花外交
2026年10月28日
广告
（德国之声中文网）默茨总理在命名兰花的仪式上表示，这对他来说是“莫大的荣幸”。
以兰花为重要外宾命名，是新加坡自1957年开始的独特外交传统，也被称为“兰花外交”。
兰花是新加坡的国花，当地通常会透过杂交培育新品种，再以来访的国家元首、政府领袖或重要国际人士命名，作为友好关系的象征。
在德国政治人物当中，前总理默克尔拥有名为“安格拉·默克尔石斛兰”（Dendrobium Angela Merkel）的兰花，前总理肖尔茨则有“奥拉夫·肖尔茨火焰兰”（Renanthera Olaf Scholz），德国总统施泰因麦尔也曾获得专属命名兰花。如今，默茨也加入这份名单。
除了德国政要之外，新加坡过去也曾以英国黛安娜王妃、前英国首相撒切尔夫人、中国国家主席习近平、美国前总统欧巴马、日本明仁天皇等国际知名人物为兰花命名。对这个城市国家而言，这些兰花不只是植物，更是维系国际关系与展现外交友谊的独特象征。

items.title: 德语媒体：代价高昂的玩笑
items.description: 法国球星姆巴佩因所谓“中国独裁者”事件而遭到中国举国声讨的事件，也引起了德语媒体的广泛关注。《南德意志报》评论称，一句不经意间的玩笑，竟引发了一场不折不扣的政治风波，并让姆巴佩付出了惨重的代价。《法兰克福汇报》评论称，令人啼笑皆非的是，北京谴责姆巴佩“伤害中国人民感情”的同时，却不打算让民众知晓这位球星具体说了什么。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《南德意志报》写道，一张恶搞法国球星姆巴佩的网络表情包，竟然让姆巴佩本人在中国惹上了大麻烦。该报以《代价高昂的玩笑》为题发表评论写道：
“在中国，绝不可以拿毛泽东开玩笑，即便不提毛泽东的名字，也是绝对不被允许的。如今，姆巴佩对此有了切身的体会。这位法国球星在一段近期流传的采访视频中表示，他认为，一幅将他P成中国开国元首的图片让他觉得非常好玩：著名的中山装加上半秃的发型。此番言论立即在中国引起强烈反响。多家中国企业立即宣布解除同姆巴佩的广告合约。一句不经意间的玩笑竟演变成了不折不扣的国际事件。
本周二，中国外交部也就此做出正式表态。外交部发言人郭嘉昆表示：‘任何伤害中国人民感情的言行，都会遭到中国人民的共同抵制。’
那么，这位法国球星到底说了什么，为什么会在中国引起轩然大波？他将毛泽东称为独裁者。其实姆巴佩也有点冤枉。事实上，姆巴佩既没有提到毛泽东的名字，而采访内容也完全和中国无关。姆巴佩只是被问道，他最喜欢哪一个关于他本人的网络搞笑内容。姆巴佩回答说，他最喜欢一幅将他描绘成‘中国独裁者’的表情图片。这是一张将姆巴佩的脸拼接到毛泽东身上的图片。姆巴佩随口说到，他很喜欢将这张图发给朋友，比如一起玩PlayStation的时候。”
《南德意志报》评论写道，一句朋友间的玩笑，竟立即引起了中国方面的强烈不满。几家姆巴佩的中国赞助商立即宣布终止同他的一切合作。
“几家公司终止合作的理由听起来大同小异：绝不能容忍任何伤害中国人民感情的行为。不过，引人注意的是，这些企业的声明都回避了一点：姆巴佩究竟说了什么。
中国足球平台懂球帝也就此发声，谴责这位法国球员的言论伤害了中国球迷的感情，但同时也申明，平台无法翻译并刊发他的原话。于是乎，中国社交网络上出现了一种诡异的场面：许多中国球迷都知道姆巴佩肯定是说了什么大逆不道的话。但至于他到底说了什么，显然球迷们就不需要知道了。”
“在许多人看来，习近平本人早已是一名独裁者”
《法兰克福汇报》评论写道，毛泽东是一名独裁者，这一点在史学界已经完全没有争议。毕竟他发动的“大跃进”，导致数千万人死于饥荒。他发动的“文化大革命”，更是将中国带入了混乱和暴力。但尽管如此，姆巴佩的玩笑还是令中国共产党感到无法容忍：
“然而，吊诡之处却在于，在中国，没有任何人站出来解释一下，姆巴佩到底发表了什么大逆不道的言论。所谓‘伤害中国人民感情’事件成了社媒的热门话题，排行榜下面很多人在追问，这位法国人到底怎么伤害了我们的感情？不过，要回答他们的问题，党的宣传机器就不得不重复姆巴佩的原话。于是乎，他们干脆删除了相关的视频。
这背后的原因是，中共认为，苏联对自身历史的批判性反思，是导致其最终衰亡的重要原因。2013年，中国党和国家领导人习近平在一次讲话中表示，对列宁和斯大林的否定，助长了历史虚无主义和意识形态的混乱。目前，中共中央五中全会正在北京举行，其核心议题就是强化意识形态和加强党的集中统一领导。这很可能也是在为明年的党代会作准备，届时习近平预计将再次当选党的最高领导人，任期五年。在许多人眼中，习近平本人早已是一名独裁者，美国前总统拜登就曾对习近平作出这样的评价。”

items.title: 中国人口老龄化的速度明显加快
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中国人口老龄化的速度明显加快/a-79788609?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 中国的老龄人口占比越来越大，预示着公共支出将更多地从家庭和学校领域，转向养老金和医疗保健领域。
items.content:
社会中国
中国人口老龄化的速度明显加快
2026年10月28日
广告
（德国之声中文网）中国国家统计局近日公布的《中国统计年鉴2026》显示，去年中国全国0至14岁人口2.1276亿人，占总人口15.1%；65岁及以上人口2.2365亿人，占总人口15.9%；老年抚养比升至23.1%，首次超过少儿抚养比（22%）。
少儿抚养比是指某一人口中0～14岁少儿人口数与15～64岁劳动年龄人口数之比。老年抚养比是指一个国家或地区65岁及以上人群与15～64岁劳动年龄人口数之比。
如果两项指标都较低，意味着社会处于劳动力丰富、抚养负担低的阶段。
中国近年来老年抚养比迅速上升。2016年，中国老年抚养比为15%，到2021年首次突破20%，达20.8%。2024年老年抚养比升至22.8%，当年的少儿抚养比为23%。
中国近年来一直在为老龄化比例不断增加做好准备，同时敦促年轻一代结婚并生育更多孩子。在1980年至2015年底期间，中国实施备受争议的“一孩政策”，控制人口增长。尽管中国近年来放宽家庭规模限制，但生育率仍不断降低。根据《中国统计年鉴2026》及相关官方统计数据，中国2025年全年出生人口为792万人，出生率为5.63‰，人口自然增长率为-2.41‰。
研究人员认为，中国人口结构的变化可能预示着公共支出将更多地从家庭和学校领域，转向养老金和医疗保健领域。
根据欧盟统计局（EUROSTAT）的数据，2025年12月，德国的老年抚养比为35.90%。

items.title: "欧洲制造"政策让土耳其躺枪
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/欧洲制造-政策让土耳其躺枪/a-79788015?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 为抵御中国的不公平贸易行为，欧盟拟出台《工业加速器法案》，只补贴在欧洲生产的汽车。德法本月达成妥协，英国和挪威的供应商可获"欧洲原产"资格，但土耳其、摩洛哥等国仍被排除在外，业界意见分歧。
items.content:
"欧洲制造"政策让土耳其躺枪
2026年10月28日
（德国之声中文网）欧盟3月提出的《工业加速器法案》（IAA）旨在帮助欧洲汽车业抵御中国的不公平贸易行为。法案力图推动欧洲汽车工厂升级，并只补贴在欧洲生产的汽车。
然而，这项"欧洲制造"计划引起了土耳其、摩洛哥、日本和韩国等盟友汽车生产国的深切担忧，这些国家都深度嵌入欧洲供应链。本月早些时候，德国和法国在僵持数月后达成关键妥协：英国、挪威等非欧盟成员国的供应商可获"欧洲原产"资格，但土耳其、摩洛哥等国仍被排除在外。
土耳其被拒门外：七成汽车出口面临壁垒
自1990年代中期起就能无障碍进入欧盟市场的土耳其，仍被排除在外。土耳其经济发展基金会（IKV）主席泽伊蒂诺卢（Ayhan Zeytinoglu）对德国之声表示，土耳其汽车出口的73%流向欧盟，"欧洲制造"壁垒将重创土耳其的对欧贸易和出口，也会损害欧洲汽车业本身。据土耳其汽车出口商协会（OIB）计算，去年土耳其对欧盟汽车出口额达301亿美元（268亿欧元）。
该法案要求，除电池外，汽车零部件总价值的70%须在欧洲生产。最初的提案只适用于纯电动、插电混动和燃料电池车型，去年这些车型仅占欧盟新车注册量的27%。法国国家科学研究中心（CNRS）高级研究员帕尔迪（Tommaso Pardi）认为，这一门槛相当宽松：一辆欧洲产电动车去掉电池后，约83%的零部件来自欧洲。
但按照修订后的德法方案，2035年后仍可销售的部分混动车和燃油车也将纳入规则，而这些车型的欧洲零部件比例要低得多。土耳其去年对欧盟出口的近80万辆汽车，大多会受到影响。
中国资本借道土耳其和摩洛哥
排除土耳其的另一个原因，是中国车企正在当地扩张，试图借道进入欧盟。斯威汽车在土耳其的工厂开工不到一年即关闭，原因是车辆不符合欧盟安全标准；比亚迪在马尼萨投资10亿美元建厂的计划也已搁置。据咨询公司艾睿铂（AlixPartners）统计，新冠疫情以来，摩洛哥已吸引超过100亿欧元的中国投资，主要投向电池和零部件。
摩洛哥是法国车企的低成本生产基地。如果它被排除，法国的平价车型很可能涨价。日本车企从本土进口的汽车将无缘欧盟补贴；韩国现代和起亚从亚洲运来的车型同样不符合条件，但韩企在波兰和匈牙利的电池工厂可算作欧洲产能。
车企与零部件供应商立场对立
帕尔迪指出，欧洲汽车巨头正游说弱化法案，以便继续从海外、尤其是从中国采购，保住高利润率。车企警告，零部件成本上升会削弱它们对中国对手的竞争力，欧洲电池供应短期内也难以满足需求。安卡拉正在游说布鲁塞尔，车企则寻求日后纳入土耳其的妥协方案，帕尔迪认为这可能仅限于当地的欧洲企业，排除中国资本。
欧洲汽车零部件供应商则呼吁强化法案，警告若缺乏保护，到2035年可能流失多达65万个岗位。欧洲汽车供应商协会（CLEPA）秘书长克里格（Benjamin Krieger）说："我们必须止血。"他建议欧盟设立"选择加入"机制，以监管趋同、社会与环境标准、尊重法治和对等原则等客观标准为门槛，并辅以反规避措施。符合标准的伙伴国，包括土耳其、摩洛哥、日本和韩国，都可以加入。

Huawei opens defence in US criminal trial, touting its record of innovation
Chinese tech giant seeks to show its global success stems from research and development, not trade secret theft or sanctions violations
3-MIN READ3-MIN

Mark Magnierin New York
Huawei Technologies started presenting its case on Wednesday, arguing that as a cutting-edge global tech leader it had no interest in stealing trade secrets, in a high-stakes criminal trial involving dozens of witnesses, legions of lawyers and untold millions of US dollars in legal fees.
The Shenzhen-based company has pleaded not guilty to 14 criminal counts in New York’s Eastern District Court, including racketeering conspiracy, bank fraud, wire fraud and trade secret theft spanning more than two decades. If it loses, the four-decade-old company faces huge financial and regulatory penalties.
The government, which wrapped up its case on Wednesday morning, has alleged that Huawei operated as a criminal enterprise that stole intellectual property – including material related to US telecoms carrier T-Mobile’s “Tappy” smartphone-testing robot – and violated US sanctions against Iran to fuel its global expansion. The prosecution has called 61 witnesses over nearly seven weeks.

US Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
The move comes just days ahead of the US midterm elections, in which the rising cost of living has been a key issue
The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.
The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 to 4.00 per cent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.
“The accumulation of more information will help the committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the committee’s 2 per cent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.

Netanyahu set to remain caretaker PM after inconclusive Israel election
The success of Arab Israeli parties at the polls leaves rival Eisenkot little realistic path to power without their broad backing
Benjamin Netanyahu looked set to remain Israel’s caretaker prime minister after unexpectedly strong backing among Jewish voters left his opponents little apparent prospect of unseating him, despite his right-wing bloc losing its parliamentary majority.
With nearly 86 per cent of votes tallied on Wednesday, Israel’s three main broadcasters projected Netanyahu’s bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties would win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, well ahead of the 48 for rival Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc.
Parties representing Arab Israelis were projected to win an unprecedented 19 seats, leaving Eisenkot little realistic path to power without their broad backing, which many Jewish political leaders reject.

items.title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget
items.description: The chancellor targets the cost of living amid global economic turmoil but opposition parties say he has not been bold enough.
items.content:
Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget
- Published
Millions of households will get £100 to help with soaring energy bills to be paid for by a tax on bank profits, John Healey has announced in his first Budget.
The chancellor said he wanted to give hard-pressed families "breathing space now" and "hope for the future" as the UK economy is battered by "global economic storms".
He also unveiled tax breaks to boost high street businesses - but confirmed that many big decisions, including on defence spending and welfare, will not be made until next year.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Healey's plans were "not bold enough" and the government was "overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system".
In an hour-long speech to a packed House of Commons, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham and other frontbench colleagues cheering him on, the chancellor unveiled a string of measures aimed at cutting the cost of living.
These include:
- One-off £100 energy payment for people living in council tax bands A to D in England, with Wales saying it will match the payment and the Scottish government planning to "replicate" it
- Gas standing charges in England, Scotland and Wales, to be scrapped during 2027 "or as soon as possible after". These fixed daily fees will be shifted onto the price of each unit of energy, meaning heavy gas users will face higher bills
- Extending the 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel to July
- Increasing minimum wage rates by 3.9% in April, although there will be no progress on narrowing the gap between rates for older and younger workers
Healey increased the tax on the profits of big banks from 3% to 6%, which will last from January next year to April 2028, and increased taxes on high-stakes gambling machines.
- Budget 2026: Key points at a glance 
  - Published3 hours ago
- Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you 
  - Published3 hours ago
- Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures 
  - Published3 hours ago
As part of a package to help business, Healey increased the point at which High Street shops in England start paying business rates from £12,000 to £18,000, with vape shops and adult gaming centres excluded from the relief.
But he had little scope for big giveaways as the public finances remain stretched, with the UK set to spend £14bn more on debt interest payments this year.
Income tax thresholds will remain frozen and the tax on income from savings and property rental will rise to 24% for basic rate taxpayers from April 2027, after it had been scheduled to go up to 22%.
But a cut to the cash ISA allowance from £20,000 a year to £12,000, announced last year by Healey's predecessor Rachel Reeves, will be axed.
The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) downgraded its growth forecast for next year to 1%, with slightly higher increases predicted for subsequent years.
In its latest assessment, the OBR said British households were set to be little better off than before the Covid pandemic even a decade after Covid-19 hit, a situation the watchdog's boss David Miles described as "pretty grim".
In his Budget speech, Healey repeatedly stressed that the UK economy was being battered by "global uncertainties" and soaring oil prices caused by conflict in the Middle East.
"Those are the storms we face. We can't wish them away. We must choose the course we steer through them," he told MPs.
Healey also used his speech to announce plans to allow regional mayors to keep 20% of business rates and a share of income tax to spend on local priorities.
The aim was to allow mayors to retain 100% of business rates raised in their areas by the end of the decade, he added, in "the most radical act of devolution in a generation".
And he sought to address opposition claims the Labour government is unwilling to cut benefits, insisting that both he and Burnham were committed to bringing down the welfare bill in a "Labour way".
But he said no decisions would be taken until reviews by Alan Milburn, into young people not in work or training, and Stephen Timms, on Personal Independence Payments, had been published, with legislation to follow next year.
The £4.7bn black hole in the defence investment plan will be funded, the chancellor revealed, in part through taking money from capital budgets across Whitehall.
Healey said he will set out how the government plans to meet its commitment to spend 3% of the national income on defence by 2030, and 3.5% by 2035, at next year's spending review.
But Badenoch said he "should have set out a plan for 3% today," highlighting his claim when he resigned as Sir Keir Starmer's defence secretary in June that UK forces were at risk due to a lack of cash.
"So now he is the man who is increasing risk to personnel on operations, he is the man who is making our country less safe, he has failed his own test," the Conservative leader said.
"This is on him and no-one will ever forget. If he had any decency he would resign again today."
The Tory leader said that with the UK heading for a record tax burden and "spending more on debt interest than on the army and schools combined", Healey's Budget was "not good enough, not strong enough, not bold enough".
Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said the Budget "has a raft of fiddly measures but very little that will move the dial on growth".
Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said that until the government has "the courage" to fix the UK's trading relationship with the EU any Budget will just be "tinkering around the edges" and will not provide the growth the country needs.
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said the Budget was full of "little giveaways" but "doesn't overall do very much" and did not offer "anything of any value on defence whatsoever".
Healey also faced criticism from the left, with the general secretary of the Unite union, Sharon Graham describing the cost of living measures in the Budget as "baby steps".
"Scrapping standing charges on gas and a £100 energy payment for households in council tax bands, A to D, whilst welcome, will not touch the sides, when many forecasts show bills set to jump over £400 in January," she added.
Green Party leader Zack Polanski said it was a Budget "that betrays the future for young people and the planet they inherit".
He added: "The chancellor didn't mention climate once but praised bankers repeatedly."

items.title: Key points at a glance
items.description: Here’s what you need to know from John Healey’s first Budget, as the chancellor sets out the government’s tax and spending plans.
items.content:
Budget 2026: Key points at a glance
- Published
Chancellor John Healey has set out the government's tax and spending plans in his Budget – the first since Andy Burnham became prime minister.
Here is a summary of the main points.
- One-off £100 payment for up to 20 million households in council tax bands A-D in England to help deal with rising energy bills, with equivalent funding for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
- Standing charges – fixed daily fees customers pay regardless of usage – to be removed from household gas bills in England, Scotland and Wales, with costs added to the unit rate instead
- VAT cut on electricity bills extended to July
- A green levy - the Gas Shipper Obligation to fund hydrogen projects - to be removed from energy bills and put on to general taxation
- Freeze on fuel duty extended again to July
- Import taxes to be removed on more than 100 food products, including gherkins and marmalade, as well as kerosene and fertilisers
- A 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for those driving up to 10,000 miles for work made permanent, with the rate rising from 25p per mile to 35p above that distance
- A new scheme taking 25% off electricity bills for 10,000 energy-intensive businesses to launch in April, with payments backdated for energy costs this year
- An extra 2% tax on income from savings and property rental from April
- Amount people can put into tax-free cash Isas (Individual Savings Accounts) to remain at £20,000 a year, with plans to lower the limit to £12,000 for under-65s scrapped
- Surcharge banks pay on their profits to rise from 3% to 6% for 15 months, starting in January
- Threshold at which High Street shops start paying business rates in England to be increased from £12,000 to £18,000, meaning businesses would pay no rates on properties with a rateable value below this level
- Adult games centres and vape shops will no longer qualify for certain business rates relief
- Taxes on gambling machines with stakes over £1 to rise from 20% to 25%
- Online marketplaces like Amazon, eBay and Temu to be made responsible for collecting VAT owed by sellers using their platforms
- New, flat-rate state pension to rise by £488 a year from April – equivalent to 3.9% - under the triple lock policy, with old basic state pension to rise by £374.40
- A new tax-free allowance for low-income pensioners, to ensure those with income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax
- Legal minimum wage to rise by 3.9% in April
- Unpaid carers will no longer lose their entire Carer's Allowance if they earn more than £204 a week after tax, with a taper rate introduced instead
- Parental pay extended to self-employed fathers and parents in same-sex couples
- Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you 
  - Published3 hours ago
- The one thing that didn't change that will affect your pay the most 
  - Published2 hours ago
- New scheme to help first-time buyers in England purchase a home, offering government-backed loans to households earning less than £110,000, or £140,000 inside London
- A new First Time Buyer ISA to be introduced from April 2029, to replace the Lifetime ISA and help people save a deposit for their first home
- Lifetime ISA holders buying a property above the £450,000 cap will pay a reduced withdrawal charge of 20%, down from 25%
- An extra £1bn for social and affordable housing in England, taking total funding for the 10-year programme to more than £40bn
- An extra £432m for a programme aimed at giving every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas
- All business rates to be retained locally by the end of the decade, with mayors to keep 20% of revenue from next year
- A share of income tax receipts to go to mayors from 2028
- Regional bodies and mayors in England to get greater powers over spending, starting with £285m next year for things like housing, transport and High Streets
- Government to work with mayors to design a £1.5bn borrowing facility, enabling investment in larger projects
- Defence Investment Plan to be fully funded through a further 1% cut to capital budgets of other government departments, after Sir Keir Starmer only committed £10.3bn for the £15bn plan
- Details of how the government will meet a Nato commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035 to be set out at next year's Spending Review, with a target date for 3% in 2030
- Extra £10bn of economic and military support for Ukraine
- More than £600m of investment in projects related to artificial intelligence (AI), including an extra £120m for the UK's AI Security Institute and £100m for a national AI Biosecurity Lab
- A £7m fund to explore a possible future bid to hold the Olympics and Paralympics in northern England
- Fund to tackle misogyny in schools, at work and in communities to get £15m
- Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) predicts the UK economy will grow by 1.2% this year, up from a previous estimate of 1.1%
- Growth then expected to slow to 1% next year, a downgrade from the watchdog's previous forecast of 1.6%, before lifting back to 1.6% in 2028
- Inflation – the rate prices rise – is predicted to average 3.1% this year and then 3.4% in 2027, a hike on previous forecasts, before declining to the government's 2% target in 2028
- Government borrowing is predicted to be higher than previously expected in every year of the latest forecast
- But borrowing as a proportion of GDP is forecast to fall to 4.2% this year, dipping each year of the forecast to 1.8% in 2030/31
- UK national debt set to rise from 96% of GDP this year to 97% in 2028/29, before falling back to 96% in 2031

items.title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures
items.description: The chancellor has had to grapple with a mix of public finances and household finances being a mess.
items.content:
Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures
- Published
This was a Budget I would describe as a flotilla of small measures.
Westminster is poring over the 150 page Red Book, external in which the Budget is printed and also what is formally called the Economic and Fiscal Outlook published, external by the watchdog and forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility, the OBR.
The Red Book sets out the measures the chancellor will implement and how much they will cost. There are 98 of them, considerably more than normal and more than in either of Rachel Reeves' budgets.
But nearly all of them are pretty small in terms of their impact on the Treasury's spreadsheets.
This gets to the heart of why those involved in compiling this Budget have been irritated by commentary in the build up to it suggesting there would be nothing to see in John Healey's address – but also why those suggesting that were arguably onto something as well.
Firstly, as expected, it was a much smaller Budget in overall tax and spending terms than plenty of recent ones have been. But there were plenty of measures here and there which the chancellor will hope enough people notice and value – and others that some will likely curse.
There are more taxes for savers and landlords, for instance, and too for banks.
When a government has promised, as Labour have, to not put up income tax, national insurance or VAT – the big revenue generators – they end up looking elsewhere if they conclude putting up tax is necessary.
That runs the political risk of choosing particular sectors who might respond rather noisily. Think of the plenty of farmers who were incensed by the changes to inheritance tax Rachel Reeves was keen on.
- Budget 2026: Key points at a glance 
  - Published3 hours ago
- Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you 
  - Published3 hours ago
- Chancellor begins to deliver his first Budget 
  - Published7 hours ago
The central challenge for Healey, which he shares with his recent predecessors, is the public finances are in a mess and so are the personal finances of so, so many households.
And there is a recurring sense of déjà vu in the language of the OBR. "The UK's economic and fiscal position remains very challenging," it says, with a splash of understatement, adding that "there have been further adverse developments" this year with in the conflict in the Middle East.
As for what happens, next, well, frankly, who on earth knows. Or, as the OBR puts it: "The outlook for the economy and the public finances is uncertain, with significantly better or worse outcomes of broadly equal probability."
The Budget book argues that "the UK economy is showing signs of resilience" but it is also true that the national debt, tax burden, inflation and interest rates are high, going up or both – and there could yet be further economic shocks that make things worse.
What happens, for instance, in the Middle East, once the mid term elections are done in America and the result of the Israeli general election is clear?
In short, the chancellor felt constrained in his capacity to act and his capacity to make a noticeable positive difference is perhaps constrained even more so – because any intervention, even expensive ones, may merely make a grim situation a bit less bad, rather than things actually feeling better.
Mitigating the bad is arguably a noble political aim, but it costs money and potentially comes with little political upside.
Instead there is this fleet of smaller measures that the government will hope gives their MPs something to try to sell – while acknowledging that they are not world changing.
Luke Tryl, the UK Director of the More in Common think tank, says: "The softly populist tone of this budget is likely to land well with the public. The Chancellor targeted groups the public have little sympathy with - banks, landlords, gambling companies and vape shops - and turned it into cost-of-living support, rate relief for small businesses and ensuring the state pension isn't taxed."
He adds: "Crucially, the chancellor may have avoided the biggest potential trap of the Budget - being seen to offer energy support for those on benefits and incurring the ire of the squeezed middle, who think they work hard but are left to fend for themselves.
"Instead, by offering support to all of those on Council Tax bands A to D, he is able to reassure them that the government will support them too."
The reaction of the opposition parties, from a range of different political perspectives, amounts to a critique that this Budget was thin.
The government counters that it is one piece in the emerging jigsaw of detail from the new-ish prime minister and his chancellor – with a plan help young people into work and cut benefits before Christmas, alongside a big picture sense of what the UK's long term relationship with the European Union could look like and a 10 year vision from Andy Burnham.
In summary, this felt like a cautious Budget. One critical friend of the government suggested to me this would be a "Mr Sensible Budget" – their hope and expectation that it might be shorn of bells and whistles, but shorn of timebombs too. Let's see.

items.title: How the Budget affects you
items.description: Changes announced by Chancellor John Healey in his first Budget will affect your finances directly. Here's how.
items.content:
Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you
- Published
Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
The help comes as prices are rising faster than expected with annual energy bills in particular likely to increase by hundreds of pounds in January.
Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.
Energy bills
If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.
It will be paid directly into your bank account.
Council tax bands are listed below - you can check which one you are in by looking at your annual bill or checking the government's website, external, although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.
Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.
This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with some forecasts suggesting a typical annual bill could rise by £400 or so to £2,100 in January the saving will be only a portion of that. Although it's designated for energy bills, you can spend the money on anything you wish.
The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was introduced in October, will also be extended to July. It was due to end in April.
- Budget 2026: Key points at a glance 
  - Published3 hours ago
Gas standing charges
The fee for connecting to your gas supply so called standing charges will be scrapped in England, Scotland and Wales, next year "or as soon as possible after", the chancellor said.
These fixed daily charges will then be shifted onto the price you pay for each unit of energy.
The Treasury calculates that 60% of households will save an average of £45 a year, with lower users gaining the most. But the saving will come after the projected big rise in bills in January.
Higher users - in the biggest houses but also large, low-income families - will pay more than they currently do.
The government wants to extend reforms to electricity standing charges later.
Fuel duty
The 5p "temporary" cut in fuel duty on petrol and diesel, introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022, will be extended to July. It was scheduled to be phased out from January.
It means drivers will still pay the levy at 52.95p per litre.
Motor fuel prices have risen sharply owing to the continued impact of the Iran war on drivers, with diesel having recently hit new records when it moved above £2 per litre.
The cost of filling a typical family car with diesel has gone up by around £30 since late February. A tankful of petrol costs about £23 more.
Changes to cash Isa scrapped
The chancellor has scrapped his predecessor's plans to reduce the annual amount people can save tax-free in cash in Individual Savings Accounts (Isas).
Rachel Reeves had wanted the policy to encourage personal investment in stocks and shares.
It meant, from April 2027, if you're under 65, you would only be able to save £12,000 a year in cash in an Isa, rather than £20,000.
But that plan has now been ditched.
Instead, the government plans to create a new "Starter Isa" for first-time investors.
More tax for some savers and landlords
If you have a large amount in savings, or if you fail to use the tax-free Isa allowance, then you will pay more tax from April.
You do not pay tax on all savings. There is the annual £20,000 Isa allowance, and an annual savings income allowance (in other words, the interest received on a savings pot) of £1,000 for basic rate taxpayers and £500 for higher-rate taxpayers.
But beyond that savings tax rates will rise by four percentage points to 24% and 44% respectively from April.
Landlords could also pay more in tax. In analysis published on Wednesday, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said these steps along with measures over the past decade that have reduced private landlord returns "collectively risk leading to a steady rise in rents".
Minimum wage rise but you'll pay more tax
Minimum wage rates will rise by 3.9% in April. It means:
- Eligible workers aged 21 and over on the National Living Wage will receive £13.21 an hour, up from £12.71
- If you are aged 18, 19 or 20, the National Minimum Wage will increase to £11.27 an hour, up from £10.85
- For those aged 16 or 17, the minimum wage will rise to £8.31 an hour, up from £8
- The separate apprentice rate which applies to eligible people under 19 - or those over 19 in the first year of an apprenticeship – will also increase to £8.31 an hour, from £8
However, these figures mean, this time around, there's no progress on Labour's manifesto promise to narrow the gap in minimum wages between older and younger workers.
For all workers, the ongoing freeze in the income bands, or thresholds, at which income tax is paid went unmentioned in the Budget.
But it means any kind of pay rise could drag you into a higher tax bracket, or see a greater proportion of your income taxed than would otherwise be expected. Scotland has its own income tax bands.
- How much is the minimum wage going up by? 
  - Published5 hours ago
State pension changes
The triple lock policy means that the state pension will go up in line with average wage increases, at 3.9%.
It means:
- the flat-rate state pension for those who reached state pension age after April 2016 will be £250.70 a week, or £13,036.40 a year, up £488 on now
- the old basic state pension for those who reached state pension age before April 2016 will be £192.10 a week, or £9,989.20 a year, up £374.40 on now
The government had already committed to not taxing people who only get an income from the state pension.
The chancellor said this would be the case until at least 2030, as there will be a new Pension Tax Allowance, so pensioners with an income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax.
First-time buyers
The First Time Buyer Isa has been in the planning stages with the government for a while.
Healey has confirmed that it is intended to replace the often-criticised Lifetime Isa.
The penalty for withdrawing savings from a Lifetime Isa if you are buying a home above the £450,000 threshold will be scrapped.
Separately, he confirmed the Your First Home equity scheme to allow first-time buyers in England to buy a new-build home with a deposit of 2.5%. It would provide them with a loan worth 20% of their property's value to help pay for the purchase.
Student loans
The government has made no changes to student loan rates - saying only that it is being "kept under review".
There has been some backlash after the previous chancellor froze the repayment threshold for Plan 2 student loans, which were given out for just over a decade in England from 2012.
It means the salary at which borrowers start paying back their loans is due to stay at £29,385 in April and remain there for three years – so graduates start repaying sooner and repay more each month than they would otherwise have done.
What else will affect your money?
Some announcements affecting your finances have already been made by the government.
They include:
- Tariffs removed from 100 food items such as baked beans and garlic, which the government calculates could save households up to £21 per year - or 40p a week - when combined with existing tariff suspensions that were introduced in June
- Allowing carers to earn more than an existing earnings limit without losing their entire allowance, replacing it with a taper mechanism instead. However, this will not come in until 2030
- Giving two weeks of paternity pay to self-employed fathers, who have previously missed out on payments of up to £194 a week for the period
- Making permanent a 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for those driving up to 10,000 miles for work, with the rate rising from 25p per mile to 35p above that
- The prime minister's plan to reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares in England from January to be in effect throughout 2027. Some cities already have caps, and funding is being given to the devolved nations

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.

Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
